The four-change sample is sparse, but its volatility includes both ordinary movement and the recent one-off payment swing, so I retain the normal 80% historical-dispersion width rather than claim spurious precision. Starting at May's 23,651.7, the prior implies 23,715.7. I add 14.3 for June's positive wage/payroll signal while not extrapolating May's farm-payment surge, giving 23,730.0.
